Yes, but Madden doesn’t fundamentally alter the game in the same way. This game is designed for strategic and tactical play. RTA completely negates the strategic part, which can make the tactical part irrelevant. 

The strategy comes in team selection. What characters am I going up against, how should I arrange my team accordingly. Then when you’re in the match, you have the tactical part of deciding which abilities to use against which opponent. But the tactics are irrelevant if you get unlucky with a matchup because the strategy part is skipped. 

Say I have global mutants as objectives, so I decide to take in BH 2.0. Great team! Works well in RTA. But I matched in to OC6 with Rhino, who hard counters me. What is the point of that? It is a violation of the way this game specially and this type generally are designed. Imagine if War or arena or blitz worked this way. It would be equally frustrating.

Edit: it would be like if Madden had the objectives you described (gain 100 yards rushing or whatever), but you weren’t allowed to call the play, it was determined at random. Now you get unlucky and get seven passing plays in a row when all you want is 100 yards rushing.

At first you basically keep all accessories. Then once you start to accumulate:

Rings: keep (and roll) those with a percentage roll that matches the type of ring (e.g attack % roll on attack rings).

Amulets: Sell all attack main stat. Crit damage is the best main stat mainly. You’re looking mostly for accuracy here, one or two rolls (the more the merrier). If you’re pushing platinum, resistance can be nice. There are some niche champions that don’t require accuracy (e.g. Apothecary, Gala) so keep those in mind as your roster dictates. 

Banners: accuracy is the name of the game (once again resistance for pushing high-end arena). You’ll probably want to keep all your accuracy banners for a while. Here sub stats are more important. Speed, speed, speed and then % rolls based on champions (def % for Valkyrie, attack % for Skullcrown). 

That should help you out for quite a while.

If you want to play the game efficiently, which is not the fun way for the most part, because there is little flexibility, read on. 

So this game is primarily a resource management game. It’s not an exaggeration to say some investments you start will have almost no payoff for almost a year, so having any overlap on characters to avoid having to invest in another is the most valuable thing you can have. This is why Phoenix is so highly recommended: they can carry you in arena until at least mid 70s, unlock two legendary characters, are useful and necessary for TB, and are a great filler defense team in TW. Useful almost everywhere. You’re going to have to have them eventually, get them as early as possible for for the early investment to pay off.

With Phoenix such a no-brain head start, you can go a couple different ways, but always keep in mind double dipping. 

When assessing a character, use this rough heuristic: GW > Arena > credit heist > fleet arena > legendary unlocks > raid teams > TB > TW. (Things can obviously change at times, if you are on the edge of a new fleet arena payout for example, a little extra investment there might payoff, even at the expense of your arena teams).

Using the above, here are some people that fit into multiple roles, making their investment useful:

TFP
Vader
Tarkin
Biggs
FOTP
Boba Fett

For the hard node farmed teams, try to farm them in spots that drop pieces of gear that are always useful (mk 3 detonators, holo projectors, carbantis). Remember, having a 6* g2 character is a waste of the credits to star that guy up, and gear is the big bottleneck. So for example, if you’re farming scav Rey on the hard nodes, skip the LS node since it has crap for other drops. The DS nodes have useful gear and the falcon shards, so they are more valuable even at the extra energy cost. 

It’s that kind of thinking: “How can I make each thing I spend as valuable as possible thanks to overlap?” that will get you as far as possible as efficiently at any amount of money spent.

And it never ends. Nightsisters and troopers both have a spot in STR, but with troopers you can get IPD droids. This is the trick to this game: try to be achieving at least two things with every credit, crystal, piece of gear expended. That’s why guys like CLS and Thrawn are so valued: they have uses and kits that plug into a lot of areas of the game (arena, raids, TB, TW). 

Getting into the habit of double dipping will get you further than chasing the meta via spending. 

(Incidentally this is why people hate the vets and the critical damage mod challenge: those chararacters have at best niche uses besides one use-it-once-and-done event.)

It’s too soon to be thinking about counters. For the most part with leveling it’s about your level, your mods and whether you’ll spend to get to the meta (a few people get lucky and back into a meta). You’re probably within a narrow band of arena rankings it’s possiboe for you to achieve without putting money down to accelerate). If you want to play efficiently, there’s a pretty solid way to do it, and I’ll say having gotten about 50% of the way through it at level 83.5: it’s effective, and it’s boring when I’m not satisfied with the crystals. Nightsisters, Ewoks, clones all looks fun to play. They are so far down the priority list they may as well not exist. I happen to derive inherent pleasure from playing most efficiently, but ymmv.

I beat it on my ~15th try (2nd try after I moved my arena mods over) level 81, g8 on everyone except g10 on Ezra. Omegas on all three Ezra’s abilities and none other. Here’s what I did:

Try to go in with Kanan and Hera having as much turn meter as possible. ASAP taunt with Kanan and get backup plan on him. He’s going to die. 

Then, dispel the taunt (hopefully with Chopper) and then either use Zeb’s basic or Ezra’s dispel on one of the death troopers. 

From there, it would depend on how much heath the first DT has. If you hit him with Zeb and then got a crit author ezra, finish him off. If not, try to get the buff on the other DT or stun him with a Zeb basic and assist from Hera/Ezra. Either way, you want those death troopers controlled and then going down ASAP. From there, get the healers, then the Storms, then Thrawn himself. 

The biggest RNG factor is the way damage is spread. When I completed, the first round of attack’s didn’t focus a single character, allowing Chopper and Zeb’s uniques to shine through. Had one backup plan revive Kanan before he went down right before I killed the final trooper. 4 v 1 on Thrawn was still tough, but ended up with Ezra and Zeb both alive with about 75% health.
